title: Scheduled Monthly Payments and Payout Plan Changes: HECM Plan Terms
content:
Five of the six Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) payout plans differ in whether they pay fixed monthly scheduled payments, for how long, and on what terms a borrower may move from one plan to another after closing.

| | HECM Line of Credit | HECM Tenure Payment Plan | HECM Term Payment Plan | HECM Modified Tenure Plan | HECM Modified Term Plan | HECM Fixed-Rate Single Disbursement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pays fixed monthly scheduled payments | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| Calendar day of the month on which scheduled payments are disbursed | 0 (none) | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 (none) |
| Shortest term of a term-based plan (months) | 0 | 0 | 12 | 0 | 12 | 0 |
| Longest term of a term-based plan (months) | 0 | 0 | 360 | 0 | 360 | 0 |
| Age of the youngest borrower to which tenure payments are actuarially computed (years) | 0 | 100 | 0 | 100 | 0 | 0 |
| Borrower may change to another payout plan after closing | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| Fee charged to the loan balance for processing one payout plan change (USD) | 20.00 | 20.00 | 20.00 | 20.00 | 20.00 | 0.00 |
| When a processed change takes effect | first day of the month after processing | first day of the month after processing | first day of the month after processing | first day of the month after processing | first day of the month after processing | first day of the month after processing |
| A change needs a request signed by every borrower | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

## How the rows read together

- A plan is tenure-based when its tenure age horizon is above 0: the HECM Tenure Payment Plan and the HECM Modified Tenure Plan, both at 100 years. A plan is term-based when it carries a term range: the HECM Term Payment Plan and the HECM Modified Term Plan, both from 12 to 360 months.
- A value of 0 marks a plan to which the row does not apply; a fee of 0.00 marks the plan on which changes are not permitted.
- Hypothetical: a requested term of 11 months lies outside the range of either term-based plan; terms of 12 and of 360 months lie inside it.
